chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allāh informed me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, who said:
The jurist al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام said: There is no rinsing of the mouth, nor sniffing water into the nose, in ghusl or in wudu (ablution).

key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ritual bath performed for major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing for prayer

ai.seo_question: Are mouth-rinsing and nasal inhalation obligatory in ghusl and wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on ritual purification. It states that mouth-rinsing and nasal inhalation are not required elements in ghusl or wudu (ablution), indicating that these acts are not obligatory parts of the purification itself.
